scope: Trader-core capabilities and implementation modules; human review routing is recorded separately in CODEOWNERS.

capabilities.boundary: Canonical version, benchmark, status-transition and paper eligibility registry. AlgorithmSpec remains the algorithm behavior/clock contract.
Enumerates current source candidates and protected historical trials with explicit status; candidate presence does not imply paper eligibility or validated edge.
Compares automatic and human-reviewed paper outcomes over one frozen eligible signal set; requires cash outcomes for abstentions and never authenticates actors or promotes a strategy.

Durable folio-scoped paper MF cash and FIFO purchase-lot accounting with event idempotency, source-hashed exit-load schedules, effective-dated terms, evidence-backed legacy-folio reconciliation and fail-closed redemption restrictions. It consumes supplied NAVs and does not verify ownership evidence with a registrar or model tax, live settlement or production orders.
Algorithm clock, cost, order, abstention and behavior specification; not promotion status or portfolio selection.

Combines registered strategy freezes, paper budget/session/instrument/approval checks, entry-zone/TTL checks, execution evidence, costed net EV, a matching itemized target/stop/cash economics receipt, and versioned OOT probability scoring into research/paper decision evidence. Missing or mismatched receipts cannot pass. It is not wired into the forward session runner, has no OOT forecast cohort yet, and never authorizes broker orders.
Adapts approved strategy versions into prospective session decisions; legacy paper strategies remain separate runtime owners.
Read-only Kite provider access and provider-specific history/live ingesters. No module infers use rights.
Provider and ingestion modules listed under module_inventory own their source-specific fetch/parse behavior; entitlement remains separately owned.
Normalize source packets and preserve event/receive/availability clocks; does not establish provider permission.
Source/use-scoped permission state and runtime enforcement; provider terms are supplied and reviewed externally.
Normalized append-only quote-event archive; legacy raw DuckDB quote archive is a separate migration/source store.

Owns effective-dated index identity, point-in-time complete index bars and same-session labels; the research module owns leakage-safe features and evaluation utilities, not option routing or performance claims.
Broker order lifecycle and reconciliation. Forward paper simulation and kernel simulated OMS have separate scopes.
Normalized prospective-session paper intent, simulated fill and durable evidence lifecycle; no broker submission.
Existing intraday Kite quote loop and its local paper engine/ledger; not merged with ForwardSessionRunner evidence.
Kernel-level deterministic simulated order/account events. Not broker OMS or forward session persistence.
Consolidated event accounting and P&L promotion gate; migrated historical gaps remain unresolved rather than synthesized.
Append-only audit/event persistence for normalized forward sessions, not the user's legacy paper book.
Legacy intraday paper trade/book storage; canonical portfolio migration is the consolidated accounting target.
Candidate generation/ranking is separate from strategy registry, execution eligibility and trader presentation.
Legacy paper signal/report outputs. The live dashboard snapshot publisher is a separate live-view contract.
Forward-edge trader cockpit projections; no broker control surface.
Command output and operator actions; command modules remain subordinate implementations.
Read-only API/MCP query and rendering surfaces; broker order write endpoints are out of scope.

known_unresolved_boundaries: AlgorithmSpec and StrategySpec identities, hashes, clocks and promotion states are not synchronized by one registry.
Provider adapters in providers/ingest are individually scoped; license/effective-use status remains governed by purpose-specific permission objects.
Broker OMS, kernel simulated OMS, forward prospective paper OMS and legacy intraday paper OMS remain separate persistence/execution domains.
Legacy paper books are not yet fully reconciled into canonical portfolio accounting; source gaps are explicitly unresolved.
The repository-wide Python source inventory is broader than this trader-core map; generated module inventory is intentionally limited to named trader capability areas.
